/**
 * The URL shape a marketing "Deploy" button uses to carry its exact selection
 * — game/plan/addon/storage/player-count, whatever that particular click
 * already knows — onto `/dashboard/deploy`, so the wizard opens pre-filled
 * instead of asking the customer to redo a choice they already made.
 *
 * WHY QUERY PARAMS, NOT A SERVER-SIDE "INTENT" RECORD. Every field below is
 * either a short catalogue id (a Plan/GamePlan/HostingPlan/EmailPlan row,
 * already a compact cuid) or a small primitive (a month count, a handful of
 * addon keys, a GB number) — nothing here is large enough to need a DB round
 * trip just to reference it, and a plain URL survives copy/paste, a new tab,
 * and (critically) the login/signup redirect for free via the `?next=`
 * convention every auth entry point already implements (lib/safe-next.ts,
 * app/login/page.tsx, app/register/page.tsx, components/AuthForms.tsx's
 * Google/Discord buttons) — `next` just carries this URL's query string
 * through unchanged, no extra plumbing.
 *
 * WHY `product` FOR THE SERVICE KEY. Not a fresh name: `?product=vps|game|
 * hosting|email` on `/dashboard/deploy` already exists as a convention across
 * the codebase (app/dashboard/games/page.tsx, app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx,
 * components/marketing/showcase/GameConfigurator.tsx, lib/kb-plans.ts, every
 * redirectPath/cancelPath in lib/actions-payment-providers.ts, the Kodely
 * partner checkout route). It predates the current wizard
 * (components/nx/DeployView.tsx + order.tsx) — the OLD one
 * (components/customer/DeployHub.tsx, now dead code behind
 * app/dashboard/deploy/legacy-page.tsx.bak) read it via `useSearchParams()`
 * to pick which of its four tabs to open. The current wizard never adopted
 * that read, so every one of those call sites has been silently landing on
 * whatever tab the wizard defaults to. order.tsx's `orderFromIntent` is what
 * makes `product` (and everything else here) work again, for old call sites
 * and new ones alike, in one place.
 *
 * Every other field name mirrors `Order` (components/nx/order.tsx) as
 * directly as a URL allows — an id here IS the id the wizard looks up in the
 * same live `cat` both sides are handed, no translation table to keep in
 * sync. `players` is the one field with no `Order` counterpart: some
 * marketing surfaces (the per-game landing pages' illustrative fixture data,
 * components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts; the /game-servers configurator's
 * ShowcaseTier rows before an id was added) only know a target headcount, not
 * a specific live GamePlan id — `orderFromIntent` maps it to the nearest real
 * tier for the chosen family, the same "pick the tier that fits" judgment
 * components/marketing/gamelanding/GameLandingCombined.tsx's own player-count
 * slider already makes.
 */

export type DeployService = "vps" | "game" | "hosting" | "email";

export type DeployIntent = {
  service?: DeployService;
  /** VPS plan id (Plan.id). */
  planId?: string;
  /** Shared across every product's term ladder (Order.termMonths). */
  termMonths?: number;
  region?: string;
  /** Subset of AddonOption["key"] — "backup" | "malware" | "docker" | "ip". */
  addons?: string[];
  /** Extra storage, VPS only. */
  diskGb?: number;
  gameFamily?: string;
  /** Exact GamePlan id, when the caller has one. */
  gamePlanId?: string;
  gameVariant?: string;
  /**
   * Desired concurrent-player count — used only when `gamePlanId` is absent,
   * to pick the nearest real tier for `gameFamily`. Ignored otherwise.
   */
  players?: number;
  hostingPlanId?: string;
  emailPlanId?: string;
  /** A checkout coupon to pre-fill, e.g. a marketing promo popup's own code. */
  couponCode?: string;
  /**
   * Draft-resume fields (mkt-011): the guest configurator carries what the visitor
   * already typed through sign-up so they do not retype it. Non-secret by design —
   * game config values (server passwords etc.) are NEVER put in a URL. Each is
   * re-validated on read (components/nx/order.tsx `parseIntent`) and again by the
   * server at quote/pay time, exactly like every other field here.
   */
  subdomain?: string;
  serverName?: string;

 *                   bot, and so the verifiable ones (rDNS / official IP list)

 *   2. AUTOMATION — headless browsers, HTTP libraries, scraping frameworks.

 *   3. GENERIC    — the catch-all `bot|crawl|spider` style pattern for the long

# Nxeon AI-agent hosting: existing assets and gaps (read-only, /opt/nxeon)

## Headline findings
- /openclaw-vps-hosting and /n8n-hosting marketing pages already exist in app/nxm. They are generated routes using the shared "use-case" template.
- The openclaw page is informational only. app/nxm/_data/use-case-content.ts says "No one-click image exists and none is claimed". Its mock shows `node --version # 22 or newer` and tells readers to follow OpenClaw's own docs.
- The n8n page copy says "One-Click" and shows boot steps "Installing n8n". But I found no n8n OsTemplate or installer for VPS. n8n appears only in marketing content, the blog, and the hosting-app menu comment. Verify before claiming one-click.
- Nxeon has no MCP server, no CLI, no OpenAPI spec, and no agent-specific plan. The public REST API has one read-only endpoint.

## 1. VPS plans and pricing
- `prisma/schema.prisma:671` model `Plan`. Fields: slug, cpuCores, ramMB, diskGB, bandwidthTB, priceCents, introPriceCents, introTermMonths, storageTier ("nvme"|"hdd"), active, sortOrder.
- `prisma/seed.ts:22-26` seeds 5 plans (cents):
  - nano: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 15 GB disk, 649
  - starter: 1 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 25 GB disk, 899
  - standard: 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 50 GB disk, 1299
  - pro: 3 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 80 GB disk, 2099
  - max: 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 120 GB disk, 3299
- Live prices may differ from the seed, because seeds are upserts and admins can edit. The marketing loaders read the DB.
- `prisma/catalog.ts` also defines catalogue data, including `docker` (line 131).
- Price helpers:
  - `lib/intro-pricing.ts`, `lib/billing-terms.ts` (VPS_TERMS, termDiscountPct), `lib/annual-discount.ts`
  - `lib/custom-plan-pricing.ts`, `lib/custom-plan.ts`
  - `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts`, `lib/vps-price-band.ts`
  - `lib/marketing/cheapest-vps.ts`
  - `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, usd, introSpan, productLd)
- There is no GPU model or plan anywhere in the schema (only "GPU"-less grep hits). GPU plans are a gap.

## 2. Templates and one-click apps
- `prisma/schema.prisma:714` model `OsTemplate`.
  - Categories: PLAIN_OS, CONTROL_PANEL, APPLICATION.
  - Fields: baseVmid, `setupScript` (cloud-init runcmd run on first boot), minRamMB, minDiskGB, licenseRequired, featured.
  - This is the hook for adding OpenClaw, n8n, Ollama and similar as one-click VPS images. Add an APPLICATION row with a setupScript.
- Seeded OsTemplates:
  - `prisma/seed.ts:30-31`: ubuntu-24-04 (vmid 9000), debian-13 (vmid 9001)
  - `prisma/catalog.ts:131`: a "docker" APPLICATION template (the order.tsx comment at line 224 says it was the old default)
  - `prisma/seed-nxcloud.ts`: Nextcloud (APPLICATION, active:false, backs NxCloud)
  - Many game APPLICATION templates in `seed-wave*-games.ts`, `seed-fivem.ts` and `seed-wave12-arma3.ts`
- No templates exist for ollama, coolify, n8n or openclaw.
- Wizard add-ons for VPS: "backup", "malware", "docker", "ip" (`lib/deploy-intent.ts`, `components/nx/order.tsx` addonDocker). The Docker CE install snippet is in `lib/guest-docker.ts`.
- Web hosting one-click apps are a separate product:
  - `lib/hosting-app-menu.ts` (WordPress plus APP_RECIPES)
  - `lib/actions-apps.ts`, `lib/hosting.ts`, schema ~4742
  - These are not VPS and not agent-related.
- Golden Proxmox templates: `lib/golden-template.ts`, `lib/node-templates.ts`. Plain Ubuntu is VMID 9000. Golden game images are in the 9100-9199 range.
- Cloud-init pieces: `worker/cloud-init-parts.ts` and `buildCloudInit` in `worker/index.ts`. Provisioning is `worker/provision-guest.ts`.

## 3. Claude, agent and related references
- `worker/claude.ts`: the "Build with Claude AI" job (CLAUDE_BUILD).
  - Phase 1 PLAN: asks Claude, using the owner's effective API key, for a JSON array of non-destructive shell commands. Nothing is executed.
  - Phase 2 EXECUTE: runs the approved commands over SSH with a denylist, a cap of 20 commands (CLAUDE_MAX_COMMANDS), a 120 s per-command timeout and a bounded log.
- Claude Code CLI install on guest VMs:
  - `lib/claude-install.ts` is the single source for the steps. It uses the native installer from claude.ai/install.sh, with an npm fallback of `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`.
  - It is baked into cloud-init for new servers and backfilled over SSH by `lib/claude-backfill.ts` and `actions-claude-backfill.ts`. A marker file `/root/.nxeon-claude-installed` records the outcome.
- Claude plumbing: `lib/anthropic.ts` (askClaude, effectiveKeyFor), `lib/actions-claude*.ts` (including claude-key and claude-console), `lib/claude-console-core.ts`, `lib/claude-stream.ts`, `lib/ai-build.ts`, `app/api/claude/`, `app/dashboard/claude-code/page.tsx` (title "Build with AI"), `app/dashboard/build/`, `app/nxm/vibe-coding` (marketing).
- Internal LLM use: the KB chat bot (`lib/kb*.ts`, `lib/chat-bot-step.ts`) and the marketing/domain tools.
- No grok or ollama hits. `lib/bots/catalogue.ts` is only a crawler user-agent classifier (it includes GPTBot and similar), unrelated to hosting.
- Marketing pages that already mention agents or adjacent use cases:
  - `app/nxm/openclaw-vps-hosting`, `app/nxm/n8n-hosting`, `app/nxm/docker-hosting`, `app/nxm/discord-bot-hosting`, `app/nxm/vibe-coding`
  - Content comes from `app/nxm/_data/use-case-content.ts` (builders `n8n`, `openclaw`, `discordBot`, near line 958), `app/nxm/_data/use-case.ts` and `app/nxm/_data/vibe-coding.ts`.

## 4. API, tokens, MCP, CLI, llms.txt
- `lib/api-auth.ts`: bearer auth for `/api/v1/*`. It supports two credential types:
  - `ApiToken` (`nxe_<prefix>_<random>`): schema line 4443, with a `scopes[]` array, wildcard support and expiresAt. Created via `lib/actions-tokens.ts`, but its UI component is orphaned.
  - `ApiKey` (`nxk_live_...`): created in Settings by `createApiKey` in `lib/nx/account.ts`. Scope is a single string: "full", "servers:read" or "metrics:read".
  - Helpers: `authenticateApiToken`, `tokenHasScope`, `authorizeApiRequest` (for mutating endpoints), `apiKeyScopeToScopes`.
- Public API surface: only `app/api/v1/servers/route.ts` (GET, scope servers:read). It returns id, name, status, sshPort, and host/port.
- No create, delete, power or deploy endpoints exist. There is no OpenAPI spec, no CLI and no MCP server. `app/nxm/developers` and `app/nxm/docs` are marketing pages (native sources in `tools/nxm/native/developers` and `tools/nxm/native/docs`). I did not read their content.
- Partner API for Kodely: `app/api/partner/{checkout,wallet,sso/token,domains/check}`, authed by `isPartnerRequest` in `lib/partner.ts`. It sends an HMAC-signed outbound webhook ("x-nxeon-signature", kodely_webhook_url/secret settings). This is partner-specific, not a general customer API.
- llms.txt: `app/llms.txt/route.ts` is a dynamic route handler. It reads live prices and the tools catalogue, and follows llmstxt.org. There is no static public/llms.txt.
- Customer webhooks: none. `WebhookEndpoint` (schema line 6111) is for the cold-email events reply/interested/unsubscribe only.

## 5. Provisioning, SSH, firewall, backups, wallet
- SSH key injection: `SshKey` model (schema line 403). `components/nx/order.tsx` (~1115-1208) loads the user's keys and passes them as cloud-init `sshkeys` on first boot. Related: `lib/ssh-key-sync.ts`, `lib/ssh-management-key.ts`.
- Firewall: per-VM `FirewallRule` (schema line 1185). Fields: direction, action, protocol, portFrom/portTo, sourceCidr, position. Supporting code: `lib/firewall-rules.ts`, `lib/actions-firewall.ts`, `worker/firewall.ts`.
- Backups and snapshots:
  - Backup tiers FREE/PLUS/PRO/PREMIUM in `lib/backup-tiers.ts`
  - `worker/backup-schedule.ts`, `lib/actions-backup.ts`, `worker/restore.ts`, `lib/offsite-retention.ts`
  - SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK and BACKUP_RESTORE jobs (referenced in `lib/proxmox.ts`)
- Wallet and caps:
  - `User.balanceCents`, `WalletTransaction` (schema line 1233), `lib/wallet.ts`
  - `lib/spend-caps.ts`: an optional soft monthly budget alert plus a hard monthly cap. The hard cap is enforced in placeOrder and renewNow, not in auto-renew.
- Nodes and regions: `lib/node-regions.ts`, `lib/region-placement.ts`. Other relevant models: `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`, `Server.addons`, and the Job table that drives worker/*.

## 6. Deploy wizard URL contract
- Entry route: `/dashboard/deploy` (`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`, `DeployPageContent.tsx`; wizard components `components/nx/DeployView.tsx` and `order.tsx`). The wizard needs login. The `?next=` convention carries the query string through login and register (`lib/safe-next.ts`).
- Build links with `deployHref(intent)` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts`. `DEPLOY_PARAM` maps fields to query keys:
  - service -> `product` (vps|game|hosting|email)
  - planId -> `plan` (Plan.id, a cuid, not the slug)
  - termMonths -> `term`
  - region -> `region`
  - addons -> `addons` (comma list: backup,malware,docker,ip)
  - diskGb -> `disk`
  - hostname -> `host`
  - couponCode -> `coupon`
  - serverName -> `name`
  - Game-only keys: gameFamily -> `family`, gamePlanId -> `tier`, gameVariant -> `variant`, players -> `players`, subdomain -> `sub`
  - hostingPlanId -> `hosting`, emailPlanId -> `email`
- Recommended CTA for an agent VPS: `/dashboard/deploy?product=vps&plan=<Plan.id>&term=1&addons=docker,backup` (add `&region=<id>` if needed).
- There is NO template/OS param in `DeployIntent`. A preselected image or one-click app is not supported yet. To add one, extend `DeployIntent` and `DEPLOY_PARAM` (e.g. `os=<OsTemplate.slug>`) and read it in `parseIntent`/`orderFromIntent` in `components/nx/order.tsx`.
- Marketing loaders resolve plan ids at request time through `vpsPlans` in `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts`, which is how the use-case pages build their CTAs (`deployPlan: "starter"` in the n8n entry).

## 7. Marketing site (app/nxm)
- The README is `tools/nxm/README.md`. The site is staging-only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` returns 404 unless NXEON_ENV=staging). Middleware routes production URLs to it once NXM_ROOT=1, using `app/nxm/_data/live-routes.json`.
- Generators (never hand-edit their outputs): `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` (homepage) and `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug...]` (all inner pages). The latter writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`, then runs a real-data audit (every page must say "wired", no "stale").
- Adding a native page, per the README:
  1. Author `tools/nxm/native/<slug>/` with `body.html`, `page.css`, `page.js` and `meta.json`.
     - `body.html` uses the placeholders `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}` and `{{FOOTER}}`.
     - `meta.json` holds title, description, anchors and assets.
  2. Add the slug to `ROUTES` in `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py`, or add a fan-out file `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json` shaped `[{"route": "...", "params": {...}}]`.
  3. Optionally add a wire module `tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`, with body()/js()/ALLOW. A pure-copy page sets `STATIC = True` and needs no loader.
  4. For live data, add a loader `app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts` exporting `load(p)` and optionally `meta(p)`. Use slots `{{nxm:key}}` or `{{nxm:key:html}}`, and use `deployHref()` with real ids. Do not hardcode prices.
  5. Add an SEO entry in `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (title, description, crumb), or return it from `meta()`.
  6. Run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>`, then `npx tsx scripts/nxm-live-routes.ts` to regenerate `app/nxm/_data/live-routes.json`.
- Design classes for body.html: `au-btn`, `au-btn--glass`, `au-card`, `au-glass`, `h2pill`, `gp-head`, `h2`, `lede`, `section`, `container`, `faq-wrap`/`faq`, `wh-final`, and `data-au-icon="..." data-grad`. Links to other pages are written as `https://nxeon.cloud/<route>`.
- Notes from the README:
  - The body tag's `class="pg-x"` and style `--acc` land on the page wrapper.
  - Keep Playwright runs sequential.
  - Don't restart the shared dev server on :3033.
- Native page dirs (`tools/nxm/native/`): about, affiliate, block-storage, developers, docs, features, free-valheim-server, game-servers-mods, help, legal, location-landing, migrate-from, mods-verified, not-found, security, server-detail, server-directory, status, tools, tools-tool, use-case, vibe-coding, vps-vs-digitalocean. Each dir holds `body.html`, `meta.json`, `page.css` and `page.js`; I listed `about`, `developers` and `docs`.
- Example generated route: `app/nxm/about/page.tsx` is generated and imports `_pages/about/content` and `_data/about`. `meta.json` for about: `{"title":"About Nxeon","description":"...","anchors":[...],"assets":{}}`.
- A new agent landing could be a `use-case` template entry rather than a new native page. Add a builder in `use-case-content.ts` and a row in `tools/nxm/routes/use-case.json` (e.g. `{"route":"/openclaw-vps-hosting","params":{"page":"openclaw"}}`). That is how openclaw, n8n, nextcloud, nodejs and discord-bot were added.
- Existing use-case registry entries: `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` lines 74 (docker-hosting), 76 (openclaw), 78 (n8n) and 103 (vibe-coding). `live-routes.json` already contains the openclaw route.
- Shared CSS:
  - `app/nxm/nxm.css` (490 lines), `app/nxm/aurora.css` (291), `app/nxm/home.css` (1441), plus per-page `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/page.css`
  - Aurora icons and runtime: `app/nxm/_aurora/{icons.ts,runtime.ts}`
- CSS variables in `nxm.css`:
  - Backgrounds: `--bg #060913`, `--bg-2 #080D1C`, `--surface #0C1328`, `--surface-2 #111A34`, `--surface-3 #16213F`
  - Text: `--ink #E9EDFA`, `--ink-2 #B6BEDA`, `--muted #8792B4`, `--link #86A8FF`
  - Accents: `--cyan #3EDCF2`, `--blue #1463FF`, `--blue-hi #3B7DFF`, `--indigo #4B2EF2`, `--purple #7B3AF5`, `--magenta #E04BD6`, `--green #3FD89A`, `--amber #F2B64B`, `--tone` (per-page accent)
  - Lines: `--line`, `--line-2`, `--line-3`
  - Gradient: `--aurora: linear-gradient(90deg,#3EDCF2,#0A66FF 36%,#4B2EF2 68%,#8B3DF5)`
  - Fonts: `--f-display` and `--f-body` use `--font-nx-sans`; `--f-mono` uses `--font-nx-mono`
  - Scope classes: `.nxm` and `.nxm-p-<slug>`, plus `.pg-x` on the body wrapper
- Game landing components: `components/marketing/gamelanding/` holds `GameLandingCinematic`, `GameLandingCombined`, `GameLandingConsole` and `GameLandingEditorial` (preview directions), `PlanConfigurator`, `kit.tsx` (shared client hooks and atoms) and `data.ts` (illustrative fixtures). This is the legacy (marketing) route group, not nxm. It is only relevant as a pattern for a plan configurator that emits a `deployHref`.

## 8. Gaps for agent hosting
1. No one-click image for OpenClaw, n8n, Ollama, Coolify, MCP servers or the Claude Agent SDK. This is feasible via OsTemplate APPLICATION plus setupScript, as claude-install and guest-docker already show.
2. No template param in the deploy URL, and no CTA that preselects an app.
3. No agent-sized plan, GPU plan, or plan messaging. Plans are 1-4 vCPU and up to 16 GB RAM.
4. Public API is read-only and has a single endpoint. There is no create/deploy/power/firewall/backup endpoint, no OpenAPI spec, no CLI and no MCP server. Scopes exist only as "servers:read", "metrics:read" and "full" for ApiKey, plus a generic wildcard model for ApiToken. The ApiToken UI is orphaned, so agents can only use Settings-issued `nxk_live_` keys.
5. No customer-facing webhooks (lifecycle, provisioning events).
6. llms.txt exists but is generic. It could add agent and use-case links.
7. Spend caps are account-level monthly only, with no per-API-key budget. The wallet exists, so a prepaid agent-credit pattern is possible.

## 8. Gaps for agent hosting
1. No one-click image for OpenClaw, n8n, Ollama, Coolify, MCP servers or the Claude Agent SDK. This is feasible via OsTemplate APPLICATION plus setupScript, as claude-install and guest-docker already show.
2. No template param in the deploy URL, and no CTA that preselects an app.
3. No agent-sized plan, GPU plan, or plan messaging. Plans are 1-4 vCPU and up to 16 GB RAM.
4. Public API is read-only and has a single endpoint. There is no create/deploy/power/firewall/backup endpoint, no OpenAPI spec, no CLI and no MCP server. Scopes exist only as "servers:read", "metrics:read" and "full" for ApiKey, plus a generic wildcard model for ApiToken. The ApiToken UI is orphaned, so agents can only use Settings-issued `nxk_live_` keys.
5. No customer-facing webhooks (lifecycle, provisioning events).
6. llms.txt exists but is generic. It could add agent and use-case links.
7. Spend caps are account-level monthly only, with no per-API-key budget. The wallet exists, so a prepaid agent-credit pattern is possible.
